payload.claim: The `passed` computation reuses only `criteria._green`'s membership test (`name in collected and name not in failed`) but drops `criteria._side`'s readability guard, which `saffron/gates/core/criteria.py` documents as load-bearing and 'measured': the repo's own `.saffron/gates/tests.py` keys `failures[].code` on node ids only through its fallback path (when the primary `path:line: word: message` regex matches nothing); the common path keys `code` on the caught exception type (e.g. `AssertionError`), which never equals a test's `::`-qualified node id. When a genuinely-failing reverted test hits that common path, its name stays out of `failed` (a set of exception-type strings) while remaining in `collected`, so `revert_gate` reports it as `passed-without-source` — a false `fail` on a correctly-written, correctly-source-dependent test. `criteria.py`'s `_side` exists specifically to turn this case into `skip` instead of a wrong verdict; `revert_gate` has no equivalent guard, so it reintroduces the exact defect `criteria` was built to close, in the direction that blocks good specs instead of passing theater ones.
